source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Providing education about expected changes, connecting the family with support resources, and acknowledging the emotional and practical challenges of this life transition","B":"A single conversation held once with the family, with fairly little planned follow-up actually offered to them in the weeks and months afterward","C":"Focusing mainly on the client's own needs during visits, with comparatively little attention paid to the family members who are also deeply affected","D":"Assuming the family needs fairly little additional support once the client themselves becomes medically stable following the traumatic brain injury sustained"}}
source_row.rationale: Supporting family adjustment after significant traumatic brain injury includes providing education about expected changes (which can include personality or cognitive shifts that are often particularly difficult for families), connecting them with support resources, and acknowledging the profound emotional and practical challenges of this significant life transition, recognizing the family's ongoing needs beyond the client's medical stability.
source_row.source_detail: Supporting Family Adjustment to TBI-Related Changes
